content: Seizures can manifest in various forms, some of which may be difficult to identify. If you experience symptoms such as muscle twitching, jerking, spasms, tremors, or other involuntary movements, or if your arms and legs become stiff, you should stop taking linezolid and contact your healthcare provider immediately. Additional warning signs include feelings of anxiety, nervousness, confusion, or a sense of impending doom, as well as dizziness, lightheadedness, falling, or loss of consciousness. Antibiotic-associated diarrhea can occur due to an overgrowth of bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) in the gut, which may happen with many antibiotics, including linezolid. This condition can develop even up to two months after stopping the antibiotic. Symptoms to watch for include watery diarrhea, persistent diarrhea, blood in the stool, severe abdominal cramps, and fever. If you experience any of these, contact your healthcare provider immediately. Linezolid can cause low sodium levels (hyponatremia), which can be life-threatening. Your healthcare provider may monitor your sodium levels. Symptoms of low sodium include nausea, vomiting, confusion, memory problems, weakness, fatigue, breathing difficulties, muscle cramps, seizures, and balance issues. If you experience any of these, seek medical attention promptly. Linezolid may lead to a buildup of lactic acid in the blood, a condition known as lactic acidosis. Symptoms include rapid breathing, an abnormally fast or irregular heartbeat, vomiting, extreme fatigue, and muscle weakness or cramps. Contact your healthcare provider if you notice any of these symptoms. Certain individuals should not use linezolid. This includes those allergic to linezolid, its brand name Zyvox, or any of its ingredients. Additionally, linezolid should not be taken with certain medications. Inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are using. This is particularly important if you are taking medications such as pseudoephedrine-containing cold remedies, SSRIs, SNRIs, MAOIs (within the past two weeks), diabetes medications, tricyclic antidepressants, bupropion, triptans for migraines, buspirone for anxiety, or opioids like morphine or meperidine. Do not take linezolid unless it has been prescribed specifically for you by a healthcare provider. Take it exactly as directed and do not share it with others, even if they have similar symptoms, as it may harm them. Keep linezolid out of reach of children. If using the oral liquid form, do not shake the bottle. Instead, turn it upside down 3 to 5 times before measuring each dose. Use an accurate measuring device, as household spoons may lead to incorrect dosing. Consult your pharmacist for a suitable measuring device. Before starting linezolid, inform your healthcare provider about your medical history, including conditions such as diabetes, thyroid problems, uncontrolled high blood pressure, a history of seizures or epilepsy, kidney or liver issues, low white blood cell or platelet counts, anemia, phenylketonuria (if using the oral liquid), carcinoid syndrome, or adrenal gland tumors (pheochromocytoma). If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, discuss this with your healthcare provider, as linezolid may pass into breast milk and its effects on pregnancy are not fully known. Avoid consuming large amounts of foods or drinks high in tyramine while taking linezolid. These include aged cheeses, sauerkraut, pickled foods, tap beer, soy sauce, red wine, and smoked meats. It is unclear whether alcohol consumption affects linezolid, so consult your healthcare provider. If you accidentally take too much linezolid, seek immediate medical attention, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for your next dose. Do not take double doses. Complete the full course of linezolid as prescribed, even if your symptoms improve, to reduce the risk of antibiotic resistance. Linezolid is an antibiotic used to treat infections such as pneumonia, skin infections, and certain resistant bacterial infections. It works by inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis. It is available as 600 mg oral tablets, 100 mg/5 mL oral suspension, and injectable forms. Store oral tablets and liquid at room temperature (68°F to 77°F or 20°C to 25°C) in a cool, dry place, protected from light. Common side effects of linezolid include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, and anemia. Contact your healthcare provider if these symptoms bother you. Serious side effects include severe allergic reactions (e.g., breathing difficulties, swelling of the face or throat, hives), myelosuppression (reduced blood cell production), serotonin syndrome (e.g., confusion, agitation, fever, abnormal heartbeat, muscle twitching, shivering, nausea, or diarrhea), and nerve damage (e.g., vision changes, pain, tingling, numbness, or weakness in the limbs). If you experience any of these, stop taking linezolid and seek medical attention immediately.
